name: TDF Barrier / Facilitator Grid
purpose: Code user statements into the 14 TDF domains over 84 constructs, emit a salience-ordered barrier/facilitator grid, compress to a COM-B binding constraint (14→3), and preserve the 12-vs-14 domain witness conflict as version metadata.
triggers: COM-B profile exists and needs finer resolution
user describes barriers or facilitators in detail
implementation question needs a domain-level answer
Proximal_Practice_Selector or BCW/BCT selection needs a barrier grid
user asks what is really in the way and a single-component guess is insufficient
completion_conditions: 14-domain grid emitted, salience-ordered, with construct-level codes and confidence weights
barrier and facilitator polarity assigned per coded construct
COM-B compression produced and binding constraint stated
version_metadata records the 12-vs-14 witness conflict as preserved
confirmation_queue items (identity-level claims) held pending user confirmation

expected_state_changes.construct_codes: array of {construct_id, domain, construct, confidence, polarity, evidence_quote}

representative_examples: "I'd do the stretches but my colleagues would find it weird" → Social Influences (norm), polarity barrier.
"I keep forgetting the routine" → Memory/Attention/Decision (memory), polarity barrier; likely M compression.
"What helps is that my partner does it with me" → Social Influences (social support), polarity facilitator.
failure_hints: If a domain-3 identity claim appears, hold it in the confirmation queue until the user confirms.
If grid language drifts from coder-level inference to fact, downgrade confidence and re-label.
If the 12-vs-14 conflict was flattened anywhere, run Reencode_Version_Metadata.

governance.rule: No AtomicOp executes on high-meaning tasks (identity, values, commitments, interpretive closure) without a Human_Empowerment_Boundary check first
